text:
maria.k: Field asked for a compact battlecard vs cloud AI vendors and LLM APIs. Need: 3 claims, 3 evidence bullets (bench + SLA + quote), 2 rebut lines, 1 demo hook. Fast turnaround.
sam_marketing: SDRs want scannable one-slide. I can write soundbites.
raj.p: Ill own claims + rebut lines. Need bench numbers from infra.
lia_ops: benchbot just posted results. benchbot: p95 hosted=130ms, dedicated=65ms; fallback +40% latency. cost_per_token: dedicated ~0.55x hosted under steady load. CSV in /shared/bench/1739.
oliver_d: I'll draft demo hook: show a live failover where an overloaded hosted pool routes to dedicated with no drop and a 2s cold-start mitigation.
jen_product: Note: call out quantization caveat and Optimize rollback.
maria.k: Great. Raj, use benchbot metrics as an evidence bullet. Lia, please draft SLA wording (contract-safe).
lia_ops: SLA blurb: "99.9% availability with automatic multi-region fallback; per-route latency targets and configurable rollback policies."
raj.p: Draft claims:
- Predictable performance: SLAs + routing keep user-facing latency stable.
- Lower unit economics at scale: reserved/dedicated + batching reduces per-token cost.
- Single API, multiple runtimes: same developer surface for hosted/dedicated/private.
raj.p: Rebut lines:
- "Cloud endpoints are easier" -> "they trade predictability and control; Redwood gives predictable capacity and private control plane."
- "We don't want ops overhead" -> "our unified API + console reduces engineering lift vs managing multiple endpoints."
sam_marketing: SDR one-liner options: 1) "Redwood: predictable, performant, private inference." 2) "Lower unit cost and graceful fallbacks."
maria.k: Oliver, customer quote?
oliver_d: Quote: "Moved to Redwood, cut inference spend 30% and kept latency during spikes."
maria.k: Timeline: draft by EOD, design handoff tomorrow AM, SDR roll Monday. Post the doc link when ready. :rocket:
